instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your elbows at your sides with forearms pointing up and hands relaxed.
3. Press your elbows into the floor and lift your upper back and shoulders off the ground.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and hold briefly.
5. Lower your upper back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
2. Drive the movement by retracting your shoulder blades, not by shrugging.
3. Use a mat to cushion your back and elbows.
4. Keep the lift smooth and controlled.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height.
2. Place your feet in the handles and assume a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width on the floor.
3. Brace your core to keep your body in a straight line.
4. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
5. Push through your hands to straighten your arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your hips level and core tight to stop your body from sagging.
3. Make sure your feet are secure in the handles before starting.
4. Lower under control to manage the added instability.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles overhead.
2. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and hang with arms straight and feet off the floor.
3. Brace your core and pull your knees up toward your elbows.
4. Curl your pelvis up and bring your knees as close to your elbows as possible.
5. Lower your legs back to the hanging position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Curl your pelvis up to drive the move with your abs, not your hip flexors.
2. Exhale as you raise your knees, inhale as you lower.
3. Avoid swinging by lowering slowly and staying tight.
4. Start with a smaller range and increase it as you get stronger.

instructions:
1. Set one suspension trainer handle close to the floor.
2. Stand beside it, place your right foot in the handle, and keep your left foot flat on the floor.
3. Bend your left knee and push your hips back into a squat while reaching both hands toward the floor.
4. Keep your right leg straight and let it extend out to the side.
5. Push through your left heel to stand back up, keeping the right leg extended.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your working knee tracking over your toes.
3. Keep your chest up to protect your lower back.
4. Control the slide of the suspended foot to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and back flat against the bench.
2. Press your palms hard against the flat sides of a weight plate at chest level, fingers pointing up.
3. Squeeze the plate and press it straight out until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep squeezing the plate throughout to maximise chest tension.
5. Bring the plate back to your chest under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press through your chest, not your shoulders.
2. Squeeze the plate hard the whole time to keep the chest loaded.
3. Keep your back flat against the bench.
4. Breathe out as you press, in as you return.
